node-1.label: A woman in her 50s presented with a 2-week history of a painful area on the right lateral chest

node-2.label: Physical examination demonstrated a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest

node-3.label: The patient was taking prednisone 10 mg daily and had not used any topical medications

node-4.label: Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful

why.why: Laboratory and pathology expert analyses converge on herpes zoster as the leading diagnosis. The crusted right chest plaque, prednisone-induced immunosuppression, and failure of antibiotics/immunosuppressants all support viral reactivation. The steroid-refractory course argues against inflammatory dermatosis, and no evidence supports neoplasm. Biopsy/VZV PCR/Tzanck results are unavailable, which prevents definitive confirmation but does not reduce the leading probability.

Expert analyses highlight that ongoing prednisone without improvement and failure of multiple immunosuppressive/anti-inflammatory agents argue strongly against a steroid-responsive inflammatory dermatosis. Thus refractory inflammatory dermatosis is less likely, despite the crusted plaque.

Expert analyses note there is no evidence supporting cutaneous neoplasm/lymphoma and no direct confirming histopathology. Although immunosuppression and a refractory course are concerning, the absence of supporting evidence lowers this probability.

node-8.label: Prior skin biopsy was performed but histopathology and VZV PCR/Tzanck results are unavailable
